intro: A Portland band, back after Furr.
story: Blitzen Trapper started in 2000 with a handful of mostly Salem kids who, in Eric Earley's telling, had nothing to do and were bored. They self-released three albums before Sub Pop signed them, and Furr, their fourth, landed in September 2008 on many best-of lists, NPR's among them. They played Pickathon in 2009 and came back in 2012. Furr got a deluxe tenth-anniversary edition in 2018, and Earley kept digging, pulling his 1990s four-track tapes into 100's of 1000's, Millions of Billions. The band that had nothing to do is still making things.

intro: A North Carolina indie-folk band.
story: Bowerbirds began in Raleigh in 2006, when Phil Moore and Beth Tacular started the band after Moore's earlier group, Ticonderoga, ended, with Mark Paulson on violin. John Darnielle's review of their 2007 debut, Hymns for a Dark Horse, led to a Dead Oceans deal; Upper Air followed in 2009. They played Pickathon in 2012, around their third album, The Clearing, which Under the Radar called backwoods Americana with better production and little growth. After a long quiet, Moore came back with becalmyounglovers in 2021.

intro: Twin-fiddle Cajun dancehall veterans.
story: Cajun Country Revival began in 2010 in Portland, when Louisiana musicians Jesse Lege and Joel Savoy met the Caleb Klauder Country Band on its Northwest tour and decided to play together. Lege had entered the Cajun Music Hall of Fame in 1998 and won several Cajun French Music Association awards before that. Their first record, The Right Combination, came out on Valcour Records in 2011, and they played Pickathon in 2012, with Klauder, who also plays in Foghorn Stringband, in the band. A Portland meeting turned into a Louisiana dancehall band.

intro: A Northwest swing and jazz staple.
story: Casey MacGill was born in 1950 and raised in San Gabriel, California. He tried blues, folk and a short fusion stretch in the early 1970s that he later called a disaster, then settled into swing full time in 1980. Boogie-woogie, swing and stride piano, jazz cornet and tenor ukulele are all in his hands. He played Pickathon in 2003, 2010 and 2012. The ukulele has since led to roles in major motion pictures, on Broadway and, once, on The Gong Show.
artist_reel_line: The ukulele took him to Broadway, the movies and The Gong Show.

intro: A towering voice in traditional bluegrass.
story: Danny Paisley grew up in Landenberg, Pennsylvania, in his father's band. When Bob Paisley died in 2004, the Southern Grass kept going under Danny's name. His song "Don't Throw Mama's Flowers Away" won the IBMA Song of the Year in 2009, and The Road into Town came out on Patuxent in 2012, the year of his Pickathon set. He was named IBMA Male Vocalist of the Year in 2016 and again in 2020, signed with Pinecastle in November 2019, and drew an IBMA Album of the Year nomination for Bluegrass Troubadour in 2021. The band his father started carries his own name now.
artist_reel_line: IBMA Male Vocalist of the Year in 2016 and 2020, and a Pinecastle deal in 2019.

intro: A Portland old-time band, here for the sixth time.
story: The founders of Foghorn Stringband met at the National Fiddle Championships in Weiser, Idaho, around 2000 to 2001, and started out as the Foghorn Leghorns. They had played Pickathon five times when they came back in 2012, the year they recorded Outshine the Sun in a Portland living room. The Portland Mercury ranked them among the finest old-time players anywhere. A year earlier, a trio of Foghorn members, Lind, Klauder and Landry, had made Sud de la Louisiane, and Caleb Klauder also plays in Cajun Country Revival. The Weiser kids still tour internationally.

intro: Quebecois fiddle, flute and foot percussion.
story: Genticorum formed in Montreal in the autumn of 2000 around Pascal Gemme, Yann Falquet and a third player, a trio of fiddle, flute and foot percussion drawn from Quebec's traditional repertoire. Their 2005 album Malins Plaisirs won a Canadian Folk Music Award for Best Ensemble and drew a Juno and a Felix nomination in 2006, one of four Canadian Folk Music Awards for the group. They played Pickathon in 2012. More than 1,000 concerts in over 15 countries have followed the Montreal beginning.
artist_reel_line: More than 1,000 concerts in over 15 countries since.

intro: London siblings of vintage analog R&B.
story: Kitty, Daisy and Lewis Durham grew up in London with a mastering engineer for a father, Graeme Durham, and a mother, Ingrid Weiss, who had drummed with the Raincoats. Their first single, "Honolulu Rock," came in 2005, when Kitty was 12, and Lewis built a home studio around vintage analog gear. The self-titled debut came out in 2008 on Sunday Best, and Smoking in Heaven reached No. 14 in the UK in 2011. They played Pickathon in 2012, then made The Third in 2015 and Superscope in 2017.

intro: A Raleigh Southern indie band.
story: Lonnie Walker are Raleigh roots-rockers with a gritty Southern indie sound, who played Pickathon in 2012. Their output has been sporadic since Earth Canals in 2015, but the band still reunites for select live shows.

intro: Torchbearers of Veracruz's son jarocho.
story: Los Cojolites began in 1997 in Veracruz as a workshop in regional dance, poetry and music. Their debut, El Conejo, came out in 2001, and a track from it reached the soundtrack of Frida the following year. By their Pickathon set in 2012, the workshop had become a touring band of son jarocho, and Sembrando Flores earned a Grammy nomination in the regional Mexican category at the 2013 ceremony. They still bring fandango gatherings, where everyone dances, to North America.

intro: A quirky North Carolina duo.
story: Midtown Dickens began as best friends Catherine Edgerton and Kym Register, a duo making quirky, homemade folk-pop in North Carolina. Their second album, Lanterns, came out in 2009, and Home followed in 2012, by which time Will Hackney and Jonathan Henderson had made them a quartet. They played Pickathon that year, with Home out.
artist_reel_line: They grew from two best friends into a quartet with Home.

intro: Vancouver hillbilly swing and yodeling.
story: Petunia built the Vipers around musicians who had backed the rockabilly singer Ray Condo, and a Vancouver band of hillbilly swing, ragtime and yodeling grew from there. Phil Alvin said they were among the best bands in the world, as No Depression reported. They played Pickathon in 2012, and Inside of You, from 2014, used three backing bands, the Vipers among them. They still run West Coast highways.

intro: Matthew Houck's indie-folk, just before Muchacho.
story: Matthew Houck has made albums as Phosphorescent since A Hundred Times or More in 2003. He played Pickathon in 2012, a few months before Muchacho, his sixth album, which he produced himself and Dead Oceans released in March 2013; it ranked No. 34 on the year-end aggregate at Album of the Year. He returned in 2018, the year of C'est La Vie, and Revelator came out on Verve in 2024. Now in Nashville, he keeps writing, scoring films and touring.

intro: A Texas country bluesman of gospel-tinged boogie.
story: Kelvin Mark Williams was born in Clarksville, Texas, in 1956 and raised in Avery, in Red River County. He heard blues as a child but did not play seriously until he was forty. An ordained minister, he plays a homemade single-string cigar-box guitar. By KERA's count, he has released about two dozen CDs, played the Chicago Blues Festival twice and toured Europe seven times. When I Rise, on Dialtone, was reviewed by the Austin Chronicle in December 2010, and he played Pickathon in 2012.
artist_reel_line: Two dozen CDs, and a cigar-box guitar he built himself.

intro: Musicians who met in the camps of the civil war.
story: The Refugee Allstars were formed by Sierra Leoneans who fled the civil war to camps in Guinea, They went back to Freetown in 2004, and a 2005 documentary about them made them known. Living Like a Refugee came out on Anti- in September 2006, and Rise & Shine on Cumbancha in March 2010. Radio Salone, also on Cumbancha, followed in April 2012, the year of their Pickathon set, and Libation in March 2014. The band that began in the camps made records at home.
artist_reel_line: Libation came out on Cumbancha in 2014.

intro: Sonny Smith's San Francisco garage-pop.
story: Sonny Smith writes songs, plays and visual art in San Francisco; in 2010 he finished 100 Records, an art project of imagined singles. Sonny & the Sunsets was the band he kept on the side, and in June 2012 it released Longtime Companion, its first album for Polyvinyl and a country-flavored one that followed Hit After Hit on Fat Possum. Paste said it mostly sounds like a Sonny Smith album. They played Pickathon in 2011, 2012 and 2015. In 2018 he started his own label, Rocks in Your Head, and the band has about a dozen albums.
artist_reel_line: He started his own label, Rocks in Your Head, in 2018.

intro: An Ohio indie-folk band with an Appalachian concept album.
story: Adam Remnant and Leo DeLuca, high-school friends from Dayton, started Southeast Engine around 2000 in Athens, Ohio. Their fourth album, Canary, came out in 2011, an Appalachian concept record that Paste and The A.V. Club both praised. They played Pickathon in 2012, and the band split around then. Remnant released Big Doors with the Signs in September 2024, a solo return from the friend who started it.

intro: Traditional family-style bluegrass.
story: Ted Jones started the Tarheel Boys in 2004 at 18, a mandolinist from Smithfield, North Carolina, cross-picking in the style of Jesse McReynolds. They played traditional family-style bluegrass and gospel for fifteen years. They were at Pickathon in 2012, and Keeping the Tradition earned a bluegrass CD of the year nomination in 2018. Jones retired the band in August 2019, after seven CDs.
artist_reel_line: Seven CDs, then he retired the band in August 2019.

intro: A Seattle trio of gritty, rhythmic folk-rock.
story: The Cave Singers were three Seattle punks. Pete Quirk, Derek Fudesco and Marty Lund came from Pretty Girls Make Graves and the Murder City Devils, and they said they had never listened to much folk before making their first record. They signed to Matador in June 2007, and Invitation Songs came out that September; NPR heard dark, haunting songs that felt warmly familiar. Welcome Joy followed in 2009 and No Witch in 2011. They played Pickathon in 2008, 2010 and 2012, and brought a favorite lamp to every gig.
artist_reel_line: Three punks from Seattle, and a favorite lamp at every gig.

intro: Laura Burhenn's politically charged indie pop.
story: Laura Burhenn started the Mynabirds in 2009, after the Washington duo Georgie James ended in late 2008. She signed to Saddle Creek and moved to Omaha. Generals came out in June 2012, made with Richard Swift, and Pitchfork called it openhearted, politically engaged pop. She played Pickathon that summer. Lovers Know followed in 2015 and Be Here Now in 2017, and on her fifth album she stripped the songs down to piano.

intro: John Dwyer's relentless psych-punk band.
story: John Dwyer came to the San Francisco band from earlier noise-punk groups, Pink and Brown and the Coachwhips, and led it from around 2004. Carrion Crawler/The Dream, on In the Red in November 2011, added a second drum set, and Relix called it their hottest work to date. Putrifiers II, their thirteenth studio album, followed on In the Red in September 2012, and Paste thought the band had matured, with warmer production than before. They played Pickathon that summer and again in 2016. Dwyer's band is now billed as Osees.
artist_reel_line: Now billed as Osees, and still John Dwyer's band.

intro: Seattle's cosmic Afrofuturist hip-hop and soul duo.
story: THEESatisfaction were Stasia Irons and Catherine Harris-White, a Seattle duo active from 2008 and part of the Black Constellation collective. They were the second hip-hop group signed to Sub Pop. Their debut, awE naturalE, came out in March 2012, and NPR's First Listen said they breathe fire without ire; Slant thought it possibly better than Black Up. They played Pickathon that year and made EarthEE in 2015. By 2017 they had gone separate ways, as Stas THEE Boss and SassyBlack.
artist_reel_line: They went solo as Stas THEE Boss and SassyBlack.

intro: A Michigan honky-tonker with Waylon in his bones.
story: Whitey Morgan and the 78's are an outlaw country band from Flint, Michigan, who took their name around 2007 and played upward of 300 shows a year, according to Saving Country Music. Honky Tonks and Cheap Motels came out on Small Stone in September 2008, and a self-titled second album in 2010. They played Pickathon in 2011, 2012 and 2015. At the Machine Shop in Flint on November 25, 2011, they recorded Born, Raised & Live from Flint, which Bloodshot released on December 2, 2014. He is booked through late 2026 and into 2027.
artist_reel_line: A live record cut in Flint came out on Bloodshot in 2014.

intro: A Portland band led by Luz Elena Mendoza.
story: Luz Elena Mendoza was born in San Francisco to parents from Michoacan and moved through Ashland to Portland, where she formed Y La Bamba. The first album, Alida St., in 2008, was essentially a solo effort. Court the Storm, produced by Steve Berlin of Los Lobos, followed in 2012, and NPR spotlighted it. She played Pickathon that summer. The band broke up in 2013, she revived it in 2015, and Ojos del Sol, Mujeres and Lucha followed in 2016, 2019 and 2023.
artist_reel_line: She revived the band in 2015, and Lucha came out in 2023.

intro: A Portland country-rock band with three songwriters.
story: denver is a Portland country band with members from Blitzen Trapper and from Alela Diane's band. A self-titled debut came out in 2011, and the band was added to the Pickathon lineup late in the summer of 2012. The band has been inactive for years.
artist_reel_line: A Portland band that has been quiet since the mid-2010s.
